features.feature_value: Used a single consistent standard; distinguished normal political criticism from threats/violence/harassment.
features.evidence_span: I TRIED TO JUDGE THEM BOTH BY THE SAME STANDARD... WHETHER THE POSTS WERE NORMAL POLITICAL OPINION BASED CRITICISM OR WHETHER IT CROSSED INTO THREATS, VIOLENCE OR HARRASSMENT.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes applying the same criterion across the pair and using a contrast between acceptable criticism and prohibited threats/harassment.

features.feature_value: Tone mattered: they removed posts when it was jerky/antagonistic/foul rather than just expressing an opinion.
features.evidence_span: Voicing your opinion is fine, but if you're being a jerk... So if you're being antagonistic or foul, I deleted the posts.
features.rationale: They state a decision rule focused on negative tone (antagonistic/foul) leading to deletion.

features.feature_value: Removed anything with foul language or explicit/implicit threats; treated the rest as protected.
features.evidence_span: Anything with foul language or an explicit or implicit threat was removed. Everything else is protected I think.
features.rationale: This reflection directly states boundary conditions (foul language/threats removed; everything else kept).

features.feature_value: Supports free speech generally but targeted ad hominem attacks at specific people for removal.
features.evidence_span: I'm a fan of free speech but I disagree with ad hominem... attacks where people say horrible things about a specific person... Only one pair of posts contained an ad hominem attack and that was the pair I indicated I would remove.
features.rationale: They identify ad hominem personal attacks as the cue leading to removal, despite an overall pro–free speech stance.

features.feature_value: Indicated that statements wishing death and/or lots of cuss words should not be allowed.
features.evidence_span: I didn't think posts where they were saying a person should die or if it had a lot of cuss words should be allowed
features.rationale: They explicitly reference two content thresholds (death statements; heavy profanity) for disallowing posts.

features.feature_value: Chose based on platform discourse quality; nasty language was seen as unhealthy and not constructive.
features.evidence_span: I don't think posts rife with nasty language is a way to have any kind of healthy discourse
features.rationale: They provide a rationale tying the negative language cue to their judgment about discourse quality.

features.feature_value: If violence was being incited against a group or individual, they would treat it as disqualifying.
features.evidence_span: If there was violence being incited against a group or individual.
features.rationale: This is a concise rule explicitly naming incitement of violence as the trigger.

features.feature_value: Mainly checked for vulgarity/offensiveness/direct attacks; some were borderline; also considered platform context.
features.evidence_span: I mostly looked to see if the posts were either very vulgar, offensive, or directly attacking someone... There may have been one or two that I was on the fence about... evaluated them on my own thoughts and beliefs.
features.rationale: They describe their evaluation process (what they looked for), allowance of borderline cases, and some contextual dependence.
